newsitem.title: MALAYSIA: Malaysia Q2 exports grew 9.1 pct - Bank Negara.
newsitem.headline: Malaysia Q2 exports grew 9.1 pct - Bank Negara.

text.p: Malaysian export growth slowed to 9.1 percent year-on-year in the second quarter from 16.4 in the preceding quarter, the central bank said on Monday.

Imports declined marginally by 0.6 percent year-on-year from a 14.9 percent expansion in the previous three months, Bank Negara said in a statement on the performance of the economy in the second quarter.
The negative import growth helped the trade account to a 600 million ringgit surplus in the April to June period, from a deficit of 1.4 billion ringgit between January and March.
"The decline in gross imports was attributed mainly to the decline in imports of manufactured goods," Bank Negara said.

Imports of both investment and consumption goods declined at annual rates of 5.5 and 3.0 percent, respectively. This compared with 10.5 percent growth in investment goods and 3.4 percent rise in consumption goods in the previous quarter.
Growth in imports of intermediate goods moderated to 4.5 percent from a strong 23.5 percent in the first quarter.
Imports of capital goods shrank by 5.5 percent in the second quarter from a 10.5 percent growth in the first quarter.
Malaysia's external debt declined by 4.9 percent in the second quarter to 12.3 billion ringgit.

The debt reduction was mainly due to net loan repayment of 254 million ringgit, as well as net exchange revaluation gain of 373 million ringgit as the Malaysian currency strengthened against major currencies.
